chapter: C.L. Burke and Kid Ory years
title: His own bands at the Beverly Cavern and 400 Club
summary: He leads bands with Alton Redd, Eldridge Cook, Albert Nicholas, Phil Gomez and Montudie Garland at the Cavern and the 400 Club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x:
That's right,
and not many tunes at that.
We left as friends anyway, and
he hired Teddy Buckner to take my place and
they stayed there about three months after
I left, and he left suddenly and the boss
called me up, and the personnel of this band
that I took back into the Beverly Cavern following Kid Ory?
was Eldridge Cooper on piano, Reginald
Jones on bass,--

Jonesy.
Alton Redd on drums, William
Woodman on trombone, and I first hired
Seymour Taylor on clarinet. After he was
there one week I got a fine clarinet man
named Albert Nicholas.

He went to Europe
and stayed a while.
We stayed there a while, of course we couldn't pull in the crowd like Kid Ory, who had a name. Then we went from there over to--what's that club?
What was the name of that club where you took the band after you left the Cavern?

The 400 Club. On 6th and (inaudible). We had almost the same personnel. This time it was Alton Redd on drums, Eldridge Cook on piano, "Streamline"; that was his first time playing dixieland, and a clarinet player by the name of Phil Gomez, a Mexican boy.
We stayed there a while and then I went back to the Beverly Cavern and I had another fine band over at the Cavern when I went back. Cook was on piano, Montudie on bass.
Of course that was the legendary Montudie Garland.
That's right. On clarinet we had Bob McCracken,
a white guy; and on trombone we had Warren Smith, who used to be with the Bobcats.
